title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, reconstructed from pp.72-74. X is a complex algebraic variety defined over a field K, presumably a number field, with Γ = Gal(K̄/K). X_K denotes its K-rational points, and Π_1(X) is its (profinite) fundamental groupoid. For a path class ℓ: x→y between rational points and u∈Γ, the Galois image u(ℓ) differs from ℓ by a loop. This gives elements f_ℓ(u)∈π_1(X,x) and g_ℓ(u)∈π_1(X,y), defined by u(ℓ)=ℓ·f_ℓ(u)=g_ℓ(u)·ℓ. Formulas (9)-(12) of the earlier pages are the 'formules de passage' between the f's and the g's and their composition rules.

The simplification (p.72):
- Take a continuous map p: T→X from a 1-connected (simply connected) space T, with T_K = p^{-1}(X_K).
- All groups π_1(X,p(x)), x∈T, are canonically identified, via images of the unique homotopy classes of paths in T, with one group π = π_1(X;T) (iso φ_x).
- For x,y∈T_K, the two elements f_{l_{y,x}}(u) and g_{l_{y,x}}(u) become one element g^T_{y,x}(u)∈π (formula 17).

This page:
- Relations (10),(11) reduce to the Chasles/cocycle-in-the-points rule (18): g_{zy}(u) g_{yx}(u) = g_{zx}(u) for x,y,z∈T_K. One checks this directly: u(ℓ'ℓ)(ℓ'ℓ)^{-1} = (u(ℓ')ℓ'^{-1})·ℓ'(u(ℓ)ℓ^{-1})ℓ'^{-1}, and conjugation by ℓ' is exactly the identification through T.
- Relation (12) becomes its iterate (19).
- The transition formulas (9) disappear entirely: the choice of a simply connected 'base space' T removes the bookkeeping between base points.
- Conversely, every g_ℓ(u), f_ℓ(u) is a special case. Take T=[0,1] with a map φ representing ℓ, x_0=0, y_0=1, and get (20): f_ℓ(u)=φ_x(g^T_{y_0,x_0}(u)), g_ℓ(u)=φ_y(g^T_{y_0,x_0}(u)).
- Functoriality: to compare different T it suffices to treat a commutative triangle (21), f: T→T' over X, giving f_K: T_K→T'_K. On p.74 this yields π_1(f): Π→Π' with g^{T'}_{f y,f x}=π_1(f)(g^T_{y,x}) (23).
- p.74 then glues: a cover of X by 1-connected T_α, ordered by inclusion with T_α∩T_β=∪_{γ≤α,β}T_γ, gives a van Kampen-type description of the Galois action through the compatible system of groups Π_α and functions g^α.

Margins:
- Top: the superscript T/X is dropped when no confusion can arise.
- Bottom: 'Autre exemple illuminant'. With x_0∈X_K fixed, one considers 'chemins infinitésimaux' / 'voisinage de x_0' / 'directions' x_0→y, giving elements g_{y,x_0}(u)∈Π_1(X,x_0). The reading is uncertain. It most plausibly means one of two things: T = a small (infinitesimal) simply connected neighbourhood or germ at x_0, i.e. a tangential/directional base point; or T = the space of paths from x_0 (the universal cover), whose points over y are path classes x_0→y.

Purpose: a clean formalism for the Galois action on fundamental groupoids of varieties over number fields (ultimately the Teichmüller tower M_{g,n}). Base points are replaced by simply connected 'base spaces', so that the Galois action is encoded by a single family of functions Γ→π satisfying multiplicativity.
errors: Notation clash: φ denotes both the path [0,1]→X and the identifications φ_x, φ_y. In (20), φ_x and φ_y should be read as φ_{φ(0)} and φ_{φ(1)}, i.e. with x=p(x_0), y=p(y_0).
Index order is inconsistent: the text writes g^T_{x,y} in 'Pour comprendre les isomorphismes g^T_{x,y}' while the convention is g_{y,x} (from x to y).
g_ℓ(u), f_ℓ(u) and g^T_{y,x}(u) are called 'isomorphismes' but are group elements, or at best inner automorphisms / torsor comparisons. This is loose wording.

(18) is the cocycle relation in the points only. The twisted relation in u (g(uv) = g(u)·u(g(v)), involving the Galois action on π transported through T) is not addressed here. That is not an error, but the identification π≅π_1(X,p(y)) is not Galois-equivariant, so this needs care later.
Minor: the hypothesis on p in (13) (π_0-surjectivity) is needed for 'revêtements 1-connexes au-dessus de X' to give enough points. The T here need not be coverings, so 'revêtements' is used loosely.

ideas.what: Using a simply connected space T→X as a 'base' for the fundamental group, so that all π_1(X,p(x)), x∈T, are canonically one group π_1(X;T)
ideas.modern_name: fundamental group based at a simply connected (contractible) subspace; fundamental groupoid on a set of base points; generalized base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Brown (groupoids on several base points, 1967); Deligne 1989 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points' (base points at simply connected regions / tangential)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses fundamental groupoids with suitable Galois-stable base points for the Teichmüller tower; this exact formalism is not printed there as far as I know

ideas.what: Galois cocycle attached to a path between rational points: u(ℓ)=g_ℓ(u)ℓ, with Chasles relation g_{zy}g_{yx}=g_{zx}
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on étale path torsors; non-abelian Galois cocycles (e.g. Ihara's / Drinfeld's f_σ for the path 0→1 on P^1-{0,1,∞})

ideas.what: Recovering the path cocycles from T=[0,1], and functoriality in T→T' over X
ideas.modern_name: naturality of comparison maps of fiber functors / path torsors

ideas.what: Marginal 'chemin infinitésimal', 'voisinage de x0', 'directions' giving cocycles g_{y,x0}(u)
ideas.modern_name: tangential base points / Galois action at tangential base points
ideas.where_published: Esquisse may allude to base points 'à l'infini'; not certain

missed.claim: Grothendieck, in notes dated from 1978 onward, already considers 'infinitesimal paths' / directions at a rational point as a source of Galois cocycles. This is essentially the idea of tangential base points usually credited to Deligne (1989) and Ihara. The reading is uncertain and the page is undated within the range.
missed.quote: Autre exemple "illuminant" : x0 ∈ X_K fixé, ... "chemin infinitésimal" ... ("voisinage de x0") ... "directions"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority/attribution for tangential base points in anabelian geometry and the Grothendieck-Teichmüller programme.

missed.claim: A clean formalism encoding the Galois action on π_1 of a variety via simply connected 'base spaces' T→X (not necessarily subspaces). It gives one function Γ×T_K×T_K→π_1(X;T) satisfying multiplicativity, functorial in T and glued over a cover by 1-connected pieces. This is a van Kampen-style presentation of Galois actions (continued on p.74).
missed.quote: quant aux formules de passage (9), elles disparaissent!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is equivalent to known groupoid formalisms (Brown, Deligne), so it is mainly of historical interest. The gluing over a poset of 1-connected pieces anticipates real-base-point/cell-decomposition techniques used by Nakamura and others for Galois actions on M_{g,n}.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly a routine but elegant reformulation (cocycle in the points, base at a simply connected space). The marginal remark on 'infinitesimal paths/directions' suggests Grothendieck had tangential base points in mind before Deligne's 1989 paper. However, it is fragmentary, hard to read, and consistent with ideas loosely present in Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: likely 'Les formules (10) (11) se réduisent dans ce cas à la formule'.
'la formule itérée de celle-ci' is correct for (12)→(19).
'Bien entendu, les isomorphismes g_ℓ(u) [ou f_ℓ(u)] peuvent être considérés comme déduits des isomorphismes précédents du type g^T_{y,x}': the marginal insertion near 'peuvent' reads 'ou f_ℓ(u)'.
Top margin: 'On a laissé tomber l'exposant T/X : g^{T/X}_{yx}, qui n'est nécessaire que si ...'. The remainder is illegible.

Bottom margin: plausibly 'Autre exemple illuminant : x0 ∈ X_K fixé, ... (« chemins » « voisinage de x0 », « directions » de x0 → y ...) ... des chemins de x0 à y ... g_{y,x0}(u) ∈ Π_1(X, x0)'. This may describe T = space of paths from x0 (universal cover) rather than tangential directions. The reading is uncertain.
'Pour comprendre les isomorphismes g^T_{x,y} associés à des revêtements 1-connexes au-dessus de X' (struck 'diff').
Struck-out line before 'Pour comprendre': '[La relation des 1-cocycles]', consistent with the transcription.
